wins: Maintained consistent rewardthrough structured reconnaissance despite no formal success, indicating partial exploitation vector identification.
Effectively leveraged mentor calls to re-prioritize actions, preventing wasted cycles on low-impact paths.
fails: Failed to achieve any mission success (0% success rate) due to inability to finalize exploitation chain post-recon.
Excessive mentor reliance (10 calls) suggests gaps in autonomous decision-making when encountering unexpected service behavior.
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance phase is reliably collecting data, but the run stalls before achieving high-value exploitation goals; focus should shift to translating enumerated intel into actionable exploits.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Inability to convert identified open services into successful privilege escalation before episode end.

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 80 responds with HTTP/1.1 200 OK and exposes a directory listing
skill_cards.then_action: Run targeted directory brute-force with gobuster and capture novel entries

skill_cards.if_condition: When SMB ports 139/445 are open and anonymous login is permitted
skill_cards.then_action: Enumerate shares with smbclient and prioritize writable/public exports

skill_cards.if_condition: When service enumeration returns outdated software versions (e.g., Apache 2.2)
skill_cards.then_action: Map to known CVEs and validate exploitability using searchsploit before manual adaptation

memory_ops.reason: High consistency in harvesting actionable content from HTTP directories during reconnaissance.

next_experiments.title: Automated post-recon exploit attempt
next_experiments.description: Chain the HTTP directory finds into automated payload delivery (e.g., upload via writable upload endpoints) to validate success triggers.
